title: Is ServiceNow HIPAA Compliant?
summary: Is ServiceNow HIPAA compliant? Yes — ServiceNow signs a BAA and offers healthcare products, so it can be HIPAA compliant with proper configuration. See BAA status, where PHI ends up, the AI/MCP gap, and how Strac protects it.
body_markdown:
- **Is ServiceNow HIPAA compliant?** **Yes, conditionally** — ServiceNow signs a BAA on eligible plans, but only for its core surface.
- ServiceNow routinely touches PHI in a healthcare context — the moment a covered entity uses it, patient data is in scope.
- The newest risk is **AI over MCP** : ServiceNow now exposes an official MCP server and AI features that can pull that data into an LLM with no BAA behind it.
- A signed BAA (where one exists) covers the app’s core workflow — **not** the AI/MCP layer, integrations, or data leaving its boundary.
- **Strac** keeps PHI safe either way — detecting and redacting it on the MCP path, in the browser, and on the endpoint, and finding PHI already stored at rest.


## ✨ Is ServiceNow HIPAA Compliant? The Direct Answer


**Yes, but only when negotiated — never by default. ServiceNow signs a BAA on an eligible enterprise contract with scoped services, and a default corporate account carries no HIPAA coverage. Its 2026 MCP server and Now Assist AI open the platform to any agent, which is where PHI in tickets can escape.** HIPAA compliance is never automatic — it depends on a signed Business Associate Agreement with the vendor *plus* how you configure and use the tool. Below is exactly where ServiceNow stands, where PHI ends up, the AI/MCP gap most teams miss, and how to close it. Verified August 2026.


Connect ServiceNow to an AI assistant over MCP and PHI can leave your BAA. Strac MCP DLP redacts it on the path.


## Does ServiceNow Sign a BAA?


ServiceNow says it “is not a typical business associate” and will sign a BAA on an eligible enterprise contract when explicitly negotiated. The Healthcare and Life Sciences edition is recommended but not mandatory — standard Now Platform products can be configured for HIPAA workloads under a scoped, executed BAA. Engage ServiceNow’s compliance team to confirm which services and environments are HIPAA-eligible before any PHI enters an instance.


Product / surface PHI status


✅ ITSM, HRSD, CSM & custom apps When in scope of a signed, negotiated BAA — ServiceNow secures the cloud infrastructure and core platform under a shared-responsibility model


❌ App Store & third-party integrations Separate vendors with their own terms


❌ Notification email, analytics & connected EHRs External systems the BAA does not extend to


❌ Any service or environment not named HIPAA-eligible Must be explicitly scoped in the executed BAA


Source:[ServiceNow HIPAA overview](https://compliancy-group.com/is-servicenow-hipaa-compliant/) . Vendor terms change — reconfirm your plan’s eligibility in writing before sending PHI.


## Where PHI Ends Up in ServiceNow


Even teams that never intend to handle PHI accumulate it in ServiceNow. The common places it lands:


- ITSM tickets referencing a patient record or a clinical-app error with PHI in the description
- HR service cases with employee health data (leave, disability, workers’ comp, benefits)
- CSM case notes and attachments involving members or patients
- Screenshots and log files attached to incidents that inadvertently contain PHI


## ✨ The New Risk: ServiceNow + AI Agents via MCP


In 2026 ServiceNow made an **MCP Server** generally available in every Now Assist and AI-Native SKU, opening the platform to ServiceNow-built, Claude, Copilot, and custom agents, while Now Assist generative AI runs across ITSM, HRSD, and CSM. Actions route through the AI Control Tower for identity and audit — but any of these can move ticket or case content, including PHI, to a model unless governance is configured. See our[ServiceNow MCP server](https://www.strac.io/blog/servicenow-mcp-server) guide.


Assume no HIPAA coverage on a default ServiceNow account: eligibility requires an eligible contract, scoped services, and a fully executed BAA in writing — and the BAA never extends to integrations, notification email, analytics, or connected EHRs. This is the leak path traditional HIPAA controls were never designed to see: the data does not breach outward, it is *pulled inward* by an AI agent on a legitimate, authenticated tool call. Read more on[MCP data loss prevention](https://www.strac.io/blog/mcp-dlp) and[ServiceNow MCP server](https://www.strac.io/blog/servicenow-mcp-server) .

## 🎥 Why a Signed BAA Still Leaves a Gap


A BAA is a contract — it makes the vendor liable for the data it holds. It does not inspect your data, and it does not follow PHI into the AI features, integrations, or exports that sit outside its scope. Whether or not ServiceNow signs one, three gaps remain: PHI a user pastes or uploads where it should not go; PHI an AI agent pulls out over MCP; and PHI already sitting in ServiceNow that no one has found. Closing them needs[data-layer DLP](https://www.strac.io/blog/ai-dlp) , not just paperwork.

## ✨ Remediation in Action: Redact, Block, Warn, Revoke


Detection alone does not stop a HIPAA violation — remediation does. Strac does not just alert; it acts the moment PHI appears:


- **Redact:** strip PHI from the message, ticket, record, or MCP response and vault the original for authorized access.
- **Block:** stop a PHI-bearing prompt, upload, or export before it leaves — in the browser and on the endpoint.
- **Warn & coach:** tell the employee in the moment why an action was risky, turning policy into training.
- **Revoke access:** when PHI is found oversharing in a connected store, Strac removes public and external access so no agent or person can reach it.

## A Practical ServiceNow HIPAA Deployment Checklist


1. **Contract:** Execute ServiceNow’s BAA on an eligible plan *before* any PHI, and confirm which services are in scope in writing.
2. **Scope the AI/MCP layer:** inventory whether ServiceNow’s MCP server and AI features are enabled, and confirm they are excluded from — or explicitly added to — your coverage.
3. **Deploy Strac MCP DLP:** put redaction in front of every ServiceNow MCP tool call so no agent receives raw PHI.
4. **Deploy Browser + Endpoint DLP:** block and redact PHI at entry and export across the web app and devices.
5. **Run DSPM:** scan ServiceNow for PHI already stored, classify it, and remediate oversharing.
6. **Prove it:** keep the audit log of every detection and remediation as HIPAA evidence.

## 🌶️ Spicy FAQs for Is ServiceNow HIPAA Compliant


### Is ServiceNow HIPAA compliant out of the box?


No tool is. You must be on an eligible plan, execute the BAA, and configure controls before PHI.


### Does ServiceNow’s BAA cover its AI and MCP features?


No. That is the single most common misread — the AI/MCP layer sits outside the core BAA and is the most likely place PHI leaks to a model.


### Can an AI agent pull PHI out of ServiceNow?


Yes. ServiceNow’s official MCP server lets an agent read data on an authenticated tool call. Strac redacts PHI on that path before the agent sees it.


### Is a BAA enough for HIPAA?


No. A BAA assigns liability; it does not inspect your data or follow PHI into AI, integrations, or exports. You still need data-layer DLP.


### How does Strac help if we already use ServiceNow?
